title: Silencing Cascade Runbook and Probabilistic Failover Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a staged alert-suppression and failover orchestration system that reduces noisy paging during transient SLO burn while enabling a deterministic silent handoff across regions. This work combines: (1) probabilistic pager gating based on short-term SLO burn-rate sampling, (2) a cascade runbook that executes progressive load-shedding and circuit-breaker tiers, and (3) an automated verifier that exercises shadow traffic before routing real traffic to a fallback region. The goal is to reduce on-call interruptions by ~60% for transient spikes while preserving recovery speed for real incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for transient CPU/memory/batch queue spikes reduced by >=60% in staging compared to baseline (7-day rolling) without increasing mean time to detection (MTTD) by >20%.

Automated cascade runbook can perform three staged actions: (A) token-level throttling, (B) per-route KV-cache-prefetch bypass, (C) regional silent handoff, each reversible via automation or manual abort.
Probabilistic gating circuit engages only when 2 of 3 conditions are met: short-term SLO burn > 5%, transient spike duration < 5 minutes, and rollout score < 0.3 (low global impact).
Shadow traffic verifier runs a synthetic prefix test and reports success/failure to console before region cutover; failures abort cutover and escalate.
Runbook automation logs and audit events are emitted to existing audit index and appear in Console runbook timeline within 5s of execution.
tasks: 1) Research & design: finalize gating algorithm (probabilistic sampling window, burn thresholds, hysteresis). Doc: /confluence/regional-resilience/gating-design.
2) Telemetry: add two new metrics: slo_burn_pct_1m and transient_spike_flag. Create dashboard tile and alerts in Grafana.
3) Runtime: implement circuit breaker mode that supports token-level and route-level soft-shed hooks (change K/V cache TTLs, pause batching).
4) Orchestrator: build 'cascade' state machine with actions: notify, soft-shed, reduce-concurrency, verify-shadow, silent-handoff. Integrate with policy engine.
5) Runbook automation: author canonical Slack slash commands and playbook-runner tasks for manual overrides and auto-retry logic.
6) Testing: create chaos scenarios and unit/integration tests, run in staging and then canary to 5% traffic in us-west-2.
7) Rollout: staged rollout over two weeks with feature flag and emergency kill switch documented.

rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy gating runtime to staging with feature flag off. Phase 2: enable gating in staging and run synthetic load for 72 hours. Phase 3: enable gated pager suppression for 5% of production traffic in us-west-2 for 7 days with observability checks. Phase 4: expand to 25% then 100% if thresholds met. Emergency kill switch: /api/v1/orchestrator/flags/eng-142999/disable.
incident_scenarios: Scenario A - Transient burst: Batch queue spikes for 90s causing SLO burn. Expected behavior: probabilistic gate suppresses page for low-impact routes and triggers soft-shed. If burn persists >5m, escalate to regional silent handoff.

Scenario B - Regional KV failure: Cache unavailability causing increased latency. Expected behavior: runbook performs per-route cache-bypass and increases prefetch TTLs, attempts shadow traffic verify before cutover.
Scenario C - Canary failure: Shadow verifier fails during cutover verification; orchestrator aborts cutover and reverts soft-shed, pages on-call with detailed diagnostic link.
telemetry_changes: Add event stream: runbook_action (categorical: notify, soft_shed, reduce_concurrency, verify_shadow, handoff, abort)
Alert definition: pager_candidate_alert -> fires only when slo_burn_pct_1m>5% AND transient_spike_flag=true AND gate_probability>0.6
Dashboard tiles: per-region SLO burn, gate engagement rate, shadow-verifier success ratio, runbook action timeline
testing_plan: Unit tests for gate probability calculation and hysteresis. Integration tests for state-machine transitions (notify -> soft-shed -> verify -> handoff/abort). Chaos testing: induce KV eviction and CPU spike in staging; validate no pages for transient bursts and successful silent handoff path for sustained failure. Canary: 5% traffic for 7 days with automated rollback thresholds (error rate increase > 1.5x baseline or verifier failure rate > 2%).
notes: Trade-offs considered: more aggressive suppression reduces noise but risks blinding on-call to slow-burning incidents. To mitigate, gating uses short windows and requires two orthogonal signals before suppression. We also keep an auditable timeline in Console and an easy manual abort path. Next steps: finalize gating constants with SRE team, complete security KMS integration for runbook triggers, and run canary starting 2026-03-15.
